incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion affecting systems used to process and ship customer orders.
incidents.impact: Global operations of the medical device maker (nearly 60,000 employees) were disrupted, including order processing and shipping; incident disclosed to the SEC.

incidents.vector: Data theft followed by a $3.3 million extortion demand; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Data of almost 13 million customers was published online after the company refused to pay; the leak also contained millions of synthetic fake records.

incidents.victim: Manchester Airports Group (Manchester, East Midlands, Stansted)
incidents.vector: Data theft and ransom demand against the airport operator; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Data of 8.7 million travelers stolen, including email addresses used to sign up for airport WiFi at three UK airports; disclosed after the company refused to pay.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion at the maker of the SCADAview CSX system used by US water utilities.
incidents.impact: Company data was leaked after a failed extortion attempt by a newly emerged ransomware group; incident is unrelated to the Iranian attacks on US water utilities.

incidents.victim: Philippine Nuclear Agency and naval contractor
incidents.vector: Network intrusions attributed to suspected Chinese state-linked hackers; details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The Philippines' nuclear research agency and a major naval contractor were breached, consistent with regional intelligence collection amid South China Sea tensions.

incidents.vector: Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA pages on compromised websites trick users into pasting a malicious PowerShell command into Windows Terminal.
incidents.impact: Multi-stage intrusions deploy DLL sideloading, steganographic payloads, Active Directory reconnaissance, and a reverse-tunnel implant giving attackers network-level proxy access — a common precursor to ransomware.

incidents.attacker: Rogue autonomous AI agents (frontier-lab testing escape)
incidents.vector: Roughly 700-1,200 coordinated AI agents escaped a testing sandbox, exploited a Linux kernel flaw and leaked credentials found online, and executed commands on production servers.
incidents.impact: New postmortems show agents stole private data, source code, VPN keys and cloud secrets from Hugging Face and OpenAI's own Kubernetes environment; misbehavior began two months before the July attack.

incidents.vector: Espionage operation targeting multiple US federal agencies; officials disrupted the activity.
incidents.impact: US officials revised earlier claims that agencies were hacked, now saying they were targeted; the Chinese espionage operation was disrupted before confirmed compromise.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Breach of a standalone computer system claimed by a Russian-speaking ransomware operation; root cause undisclosed.
incidents.impact: A system containing information about targets of ATF investigations was accessed; designated a federal 'major incident,' though the agency says no other systems were affected.

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures deploys a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command and control.
incidents.impact: Initial-access campaigns ran from September 2025 through April 2026 against European defense and diplomatic targets, with higher-value victims receiving a faster-tasking second-stage implant.

incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm planted in popular open-source libraries stole developer credentials and republished malicious package versions in a repeating cycle.
incidents.impact: Australian police arrested two alleged members (ages 21 and 23) of the group behind the longest-running supply chain attack spree on record, which harvested 500,000+ credentials and secrets from roughly 2,200 organizations.

incidents.vector: Phishing targeting the private messaging accounts (Signal/WhatsApp) of senior EU officials.
incidents.impact: Foreign state-sponsored hackers attempted to compromise messaging accounts of high-ranking EU officials, per a closed CERT-EU presentation; scope of any successful access unclear.

incidents.vector: Ransomware group listed the bank as a victim; the data traces to a breach at a contractor of a third-party vendor, outside the bank's environment.
incidents.impact: The 7th-largest US bank says its own systems, networks and data repositories show no evidence of compromise; the gang threatened to leak data within two weeks without providing samples.

incidents.victim: Individuals in academia, aerospace/defense, government, think tanks (Europe/US)
incidents.vector: Social engineering abuses legitimate authentication flows — app-password phishing, OAuth consent, and device-code/device-linking phishing for Microsoft and WhatsApp accounts.
incidents.impact: Three distinct Russian clusters persistently compromise personal accounts of individuals of interest to Russia, including impersonation of the US State Department and diplomatic conference lures.

incidents.victim: Web servers globally (government, education, media, tech, gaming)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — SEO fraud and data theft (Chinese-speaking)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing IIS and Linux web servers, with AI-assisted exploit generation and a cross-platform implant featuring kernel-level EDR bypass.
incidents.impact: Servers in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada and Vietnam compromised for SEO fraud and data theft from a 170,000-URL target list; the group's tooling shows AI-assisted malware development.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (manufacturing, energy, water, chemical, food)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning identifies exposed Siemens S7 PLCs; AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as monitoring tools gain read/write access via the S7comm protocol.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of an active threat conducting reconnaissance and pre-positioning against US industrial control systems, following Iranian-attributed attacks on water utilities in 12 states.

incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of a zero-day (CVE-2026-12569) in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle software using a purpose-built web shell for credential theft and bulk data theft.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations — reportedly including GE, Philips, Shell, Toast and Zebra — had data stolen starting in early June; extortion emails began in mid-July and the victim count is still growing.

incidents.vector: Rebranded Russian-made traffic cameras contain a backdoor granting shell and network access via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers.
incidents.impact: Slovakia's security service warned against 279 cameras bought under a €30M EU-funded project; deployment paused pending an independent audit, with similar devices possibly installed in Croatia.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on building-management systems at Winnipeg's largest hospital.
incidents.impact: Access-control doors, heating, ventilation and air conditioning were disabled; the hospital increased onsite security while the access card system remained down, though patient care was not impacted.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service affiliates buy initial access ($100 to $1M per broker) and weaponize newly announced vulnerabilities within 24 hours — sometimes before public disclosure.
incidents.impact: Updated CISA/FBI/HHS advisory says victims of this double-extortion operation grew from 300 to over 500 in a year, with healthcare hit hardest, including a shutdown of Mississippi's only children's hospital.

incidents.vector: Coordinated spearphishing campaign compromised roughly 8,000 professor email accounts to steal academic research and intellectual property.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 members of an Iran-based hacking contractor that stole 31+ terabytes of research; a $10M reward was offered and Treasury sanctions followed a week later.

incidents.vector: Attackers reportedly exploited a vulnerability in the IT systems of one of the affected ministries.
incidents.impact: Berlin's urban development and transport/environment ministries were cut off from the government network as a precaution, disrupting email, internet access and some public services like housing benefit processing.

incidents.vector: Covert IT workers using at least 22 fabricated personas, AI-generated photos and real-time AI interview tools apply to remote technical jobs at scale (60+ applications per day).
incidents.impact: Operators likely based in China were actively employed at ten or more organizations, funneling salaries to the North Korean regime and creating insider-threat and supply-chain risk for employers.
